To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of income is affected most by trade policies that promote the development of exportable activities, and that this effect is more marked in the case of the poor.

the distribution of income is affected by the choice of trade strategy, that the effects on income distribution are more marked for the lower-income groups, and that the effects are greater when the domestic production meets the intermediate import requirements of the economy.

the impact of trade on income distribution in Mexico depends on: (1) the degree of complementarity of the traded goods with the non-traded goods; and (2) whether the traded goods are importable or exportable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of trade policies on the distribution of incomes.
the effects of trade policies on income distribution and the impact of the distribution of income on trade strategies.
the effects of trade policies on the structure of production, and the implications of this on income distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of trade on the income of the lower income groups depends on the structure of domestic production, and that this structure is itself dependent on the trade policy pursued.
the effects on distribution are not as important as the effects of trade on production and employment.
, while export promotion may be a necessary condition for the growth of a developing country, it is not a sufficient one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of Mexico, the distribution of income is not affected significantly by the choice of a trade strategy, and the only way to increase the share of factor income of the poor would be to increase their participation in the labour force.

the poor benefit from trade strategies which promote exportable activities, provided that the expansion of such activities does not lead to an increase in the importation of intermediate goods, but that the poor are not affected by trade strategies which promote import-substituting activities.
the impact on income distribution of alternative trade strategies depends upon whether the domestic production of intermediate inputs is taken into consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of trade strategies on the distribution of factor income are not necessarily as straightforward as is often assumed in the literature.
, if the aim is to reduce the poverty of the poor, it is important to consider not just direct, but also indirect effects of trade policies.
the distribution of income is a function of trade strategies and that the latter should be designed to take into account the full spectrum of import substitution possibilities.
